records.title: Protocol for isolation and culture establishment of adult murine neural stem cells using tissue grinder and dissociator-based mechanical dissociation.
records.abstract: Here, we present an enzyme-free workflow for isolating murine adult neural stem cells (aNSCs) using tissue grinder- and dissociator-based mechanical dissociation (TIGR-MD). We describe dissection of the dentate gyrus and subventricular zone, mechanical tissue dissociation, cell recovery, and establishment of primary neurosphere cultures. We further provide procedures for neurosphere maintenance, passaging, and validation. TIGR-MD avoids enzymatic exposure during initial tissue dissociation and supports standardized establishment of primary murine aNSC cultures.

records.title: Protocol for simulating cell-contact dynamics of proliferating epithelia using the vertex model.
records.abstract: Vertex models simulate epithelial mechanics at single-cell resolution but represent cell division as a single in-plane split, agnostic to the differential apicobasal geometry of mitotic cells. Here, we present a protocol that simulates basal mitosis as two sequential changes: basal-cell diminution followed by daughter-cell reinsertion. Apical-side simulations can be performed with minimal code modification. We provide instructions for generating initial configurations, running simulations, and quantifying mechanical and topological rearrangements using command-line operations accessible to experimental biologists. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Ramanathan et al.1.

records.title: Curcumin analogue FLLL32 induces ferroptosis by targeting the STAT3-GPX4/SLC40A1 axis in colorectal cancer.
records.abstract: FLLL32 is a curcumin analogue with reported anti-tumor activity, mainly through inhibition of signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) signaling and induction of apoptosis. However, whether FLLL32 regulates ferroptosis in colorectal cancer (CRC) and the underlying mechanism remain unclear. Here, using a patient-derived CRC organoid screening platform, we identified FLLL32 as a potent anti-CRC compound. FLLL32 suppressed CRC organoid growth, inhibited CRC cell proliferation and migration in vitro, and inhibited xenograft tumor growth in vivo. In parallel, FLLL32 induced ferroptosis-associated iron accumulation, reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial morphological and functional abnormalities. The ferroptosis inhibitor Ferrostatin-1 markedly restored FLLL32-impaired cell viability and reduced ROS, whereas the apoptosis inhibitor Z-VAD-FMK showed weaker protection. These findings suggest that ferroptosis is a major contributor to FLLL32-induced cell death, although apoptotic features are also present. Mechanistically, FLLL32 interacted with STAT3, and Glu638 and Met726 contributed to the FLLL32-STAT3 interaction. FLLL32 also suppressed STAT3 Tyr705 phosphorylation and nuclear signaling, thereby disrupting pSTAT3-mediated transcriptional regulation of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and solute carrier family 40 member 1 (SLC40A1), weakening lipid peroxide detoxification and cellular iron efflux, promoting intracellular iron accumulation, and enhancing ferroptosis in CRC cells. These findings define a STAT3-GPX4/SLC40A1-dependent mechanism underlying the anti-CRC activity of FLLL32 and support further investigation of STAT3-associated ferroptosis regulation as a potential therapeutic vulnerability in CRC.

records.title: Engineered Vascularization: Neurovascular Niche Remodeling Enables Biomimetic Brain Organoids for Central Nervous System Research.
records.abstract: Preclinical central nervous system (CNS) disease models face a persistent translational gap arising from interspecies differences and limited representation of the human neurovascular microenvironment. Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived brain organoids provide a human-relevant platform for modeling brain development and disease, but limited vascularization restricts tissue growth, maturation, and neurovascular function. Engineering approaches, including genetic engineering, biomaterials, 3D bioprinting, and organ-on-a-chip technologies, enable greater control over vascular specification, spatial organization, extracellular matrix properties, and perfusion, facilitating more controlled remodeling of the neurovascular niche. This Review summarizes recent advances in engineered vascularization of brain organoids, focusing on engineering strategies, biological outcomes, and applications in neurodevelopmental research, CNS disease modeling, and preclinical drug screening. Particular emphasis is placed on evaluating vascularization using complementary evidence rather than individual vascular markers. Based on quantitative data from 13 published studies, we propose the Multidimensional Quality Assessment Framework for Vascularized Brain Organoids (MQAF-VBO) and highlight relationships between engineering parameters and biological outcomes. Emerging opportunities in nanoengineered biomaterials, programmable platforms, spatial profiling, integrated biosensing, and adaptive bioelectronic systems are also discussed. Collectively, these advances may facilitate the development of more reproducible and physiologically relevant vascularized brain organoids for CNS disease modeling and preclinical drug evaluation.

records.title: An integrated human forebrain organoid reveals microglia-mediated CD8+ T cell recruitment and neuroimmune dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease pathology.
records.abstract: Genetic evidence implicates immune dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the neuroimmune mechanisms operating in human tissue remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a modular human forebrain organoid platform that systematically integrates human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived microglia and CD8+ T cells to reconstitute multicellular AD pathology. This system enables functional interrogation of both innate and adaptive immune components in a human-relevant context. Using this platform, we demonstrate that microglia mediate amyloid-β clearance and neuronal maturation but also drive inflammatory activation and recruit CD8+ T cells through CCL4/5 signaling via CCR1/5 and CXCR3, establishing a neuroinflammatory feedback loop. Pharmacological targeting of CCR5 or CXCR3 blocks T cell recruitment and modulates autophagy in a microglia-dependent manner. This modular organoid platform provides a versatile tool for dissecting neuron-immune interactions and enables cell-type-specific therapeutic screening in human neuroinflammatory disease models.

records.title: Defining GRAMD2 expression in the alveolar epithelium using organoid and single cell approaches.
records.abstract: Alveolar epithelial regeneration is critical for normal lung function and disrupted in disease. Precise identification of alveolar epithelial cell populations, particularly type I (AT1) cells, remains a barrier to understanding alveolar homeostasis and repair. We previously identified GRAM domain-containing 2 (GRAMD2) as enriched in distal alveolar epithelium, with predominant expression in type I (AT1) cells. However, recent single-cell datasets reveal low level Gramd2 transcripts in other lung epithelial populations raising questions about specificity. To address this, we performed immunofluorescence of whole lung and cytospins of GFPhigh cells from Gramd2CreERT2;mTmG mice. Cre-induced lineage labeling predominantly marked cells expressing established AT1 markers, with minimal labeling of AT2 or club cells. GFPhigh cells were enriched for AT1 cells and formed organoids in culture that over time showed expression of AT2 and airway markers, suggesting plasticity. Despite apparent purity of the GFPhigh population by immunostaining, single-cell RNAseq identified AT2 cells and a small number of club cells in the labeled population, revealing discordance between GRAMD2 transcript and protein expression. Gramd2CreERT2;mTmG mice enable enrichment of AT1 cells but have limitations for definitive lineage tracing.

records.title: Virtual cells: progress and challenges from mechanistic modeling to data-driven integration.
records.abstract: Virtual cells aim to represent cellular states computationally and predict responses to genetic, chemical, environmental, temporal, and spatial conditions. For comparative purposes, this review uses state encoding (E), state transition (T), and observation decoding (D) as a conceptual abstraction spanning explicit mechanistic models, data-driven foundation and perturbation models, multimodal systems, and spatial and multiscale simulation. We examine model boundaries, data foundations, resource disclosure, out-of-distribution evaluation, causal evidence, and experimental validation. Independent benchmarks show that parameter count and training-set size do not automatically yield robust out-of-distribution generalization, while transcriptomic representations alone do not capture the full functional state of a cell. Trustworthy virtual cells will require perturbation-responsive transitions, cross-modal alignment, continuous-time dynamics, mechanistic constraints, calibrated uncertainty, independent experimental validation, and, where appropriate, closed-loop experimental feedback.

records.title: Progress of metabolomics-centric multi-omics research in medicine.
records.abstract: Metabolomics reveals molecular changes at the metabolic level during biological processes. Recent advancements, particularly through integration with other omics and artificial intelligence (AI), are advancing metabolic data analysis and multi-omics interpretation. This review introduces a "metabolomics-centric" paradigm as a conceptual framework for multi-omics integration, positioning metabolic readouts as the functional anchor for interpreting genotype-phenotype relationships. It also chronicles the evolution and medical applications of integration technologies. Our discussion first traces the field's evolution from bulk to single-cell and spatial methodologies, next surveys integration strategies to uncover mechanistic insights, and finally examines how AI-driven multimodal data integration and AI-optimized metabolomics workflows tackle persistent biological and computational challenges. Looking forward, this review identifies the AI virtual cell as a pivotal future direction for metabolomics-based multi-omics integration, calling for increased attention to its development to simulate dynamic molecular phenotypic networks within a multi-omics context.

records.title: Emerging frontiers for AI in single-cell genomics.
records.abstract: We are just over a decade into the single-cell revolution in biology, which has been coupled to the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in single-cell genomics. Most early single-cell RNA embedding models and subsequent "foundation models"-representational models pretrained on large single-cell datasets-did not gain wide traction among experimental biologists. However, as massive single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlas efforts ramp up, there is a clear rationale for exploiting AI models to interpret new datasets in the context of vast existing data resources. Meanwhile, the advent of single-cell epigenetic/multiomic assays and Perturb-seq technologies presents new opportunities for AI modeling. Here, we review AI embedding and foundation models for scRNA-seq and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq), extensive machine-learning efforts to exploit single-cell multiome in regulatory genomics, and AI strategies to learn "virtual cell" models from Perturb-seq, ending with a description of current limitations of single-cell AI models and an outlook for future advances.

records.title: Dynamic Graph Prior-Guided Latent Adaptation for Generalizable Single-Cell Perturbation Response Prediction.
records.abstract: Predicting transcriptional responses to drug perturbations in unseen cellular contexts is a central challenge in single-cell perturbation modeling. This challenge creates a need for models that combine flexible state transitions with structured biological prior knowledge. Existing data-driven models often struggle to generalize across unseen cell types, while many prior-based models rely on static biological graphs without explicitly conditioning prior influence on perturbation-specific target support. We propose DGP-LA, a dynamic graph-prior latent adaptation framework that refines biological priors and injects them as gated latent corrections within a cell-state-conditioned transition model. DGP-LA couples a transition backbone with perturbation-conditioned sparse graph refinement. It propagates gene-aligned target support over the refined graph and selectively injects the resulting topology-aware signal into the hidden representation. On Tahoe and NeurIPS, DGP-LA improves Pearson Delta relative to State by 8.7% and 35.8% for generalization across unseen cell types. In zero-shot drug perturbation response prediction on unseen cell types, it improves Pearson Delta relative to CRISP by 79.1% and 67.6%. The model also improves DE-gene recovery, response discrimination, and Hallmark pathway recovery, supporting adaptive latent integration of biological priors for more generalizable and biologically interpretable perturbation modeling. DGP-LA's source code and reproducibility materials are available at https://github.com/bieyl/DGP-LA and archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22155398. Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

records.title: Benchmarking biological knowledge-graph priors against single-cell foundation models for Perturb-seq prediction.
records.abstract: Perturb-seq prediction increasingly relies on either biological graph priors or single-cell foundation models, but their relative value is difficult to interpret when architectures, split definitions and graph sources vary simultaneously. We benchmarked STRING functional associations and Gene Ontology co-annotation against dense, self-edge-only and exact-degree-rewired supports in one fixed graph-attention backbone, with a separate 200-HVG STRING-GO-control-co-expression sensitivity. Four public Perturb-seq datasets, three nested gene-space scales and three optimisation seeds were evaluated on held-out guide conditions; GEARS, scGPT and Geneformer were evaluated on the same held-out conditions, output-gene panels and Pearson-r metric after model-specific validity checks. At 200 highly variable genes, STRING-GO improved the equal-dataset Pearson r by +0.016 (95% interval [+0.010, +0.022]) relative to dense support. Dataset effects were positive in Adamson (+0.017), Norman (+0.015), Replogle K562 (+0.017) and Replogle RPE1 (+0.014), and 122/200 guide conditions improved (0.61 [0.54,0.68]). The top-20-gene Jaccard difference was +0.009 [+0.006,+0.012]. STRING-GO exceeded self-edge-only support by +0.024 [+0.018,+0.029] and the mean of ten exact-degree rewires by +0.011 [+0.005,+0.017]. The native-panel effect declined from +0.016 at 200 genes to +0.009 at 1000 genes; the 1000-200 interaction was -0.006 [-0.011,-0.002]. The primary graph-support comparison was formulated and conducted during peer-review revision rather than planned as an a priori confirmatory study. All three external models passed implementation-specific checks. Across 36 protocol-matched dataset-scale contrasts, 32 were within the descriptive ±0.030 reference envelope and four were outside, all favouring the external model. These results demonstrate a modest empirical predictive improvement under the evaluated matched protocol; they do not by themselves establish practical biological relevance.

records.title: AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing: from genome mining to the artificial intelligence virtual cell.
records.abstract: Fungi are important chassis organisms for sustainable biomanufacturing owing to their strong secretion capacity, metabolic diversity, and adaptability to industrial processes. Driven by the rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), computational approaches that enable machines to learn patterns from data and make predictions, together with omics technologies and synthetic biology, data- and model-driven strategies are increasingly reshaping fungal cell factory design and optimization. This review summarizes recent advances in AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing, covering AI-assisted genome mining, enzyme and pathway analysis, genome editing, metabolic network modeling, and intelligent fermentation control. The review further highlights the emerging concept of the artificial intelligence virtual cell (AIVC), which integrates multi-omics data, mechanistic modeling, and machine learning-based approaches into a unified multiscale framework for simulating dynamic cellular behaviors. The technical foundations and potential applications of AIVC in fungal metabolic engineering, drug discovery, agriculture, and environmental biotechnology are reviewed. Finally, key challenges-data quality and standardization, cross-scale model integration and interpretability, and the gap between in silico prediction and experimental validation-are highlighted. This review provides a systematic perspective on the role of AI and virtual cell technologies in advancing next generation fungal biotechnology.

records.title: Editing Enzymes with Multiscale Metal-Based Components.
records.abstract: Enzymes are powerful natural catalysts distinguished by high efficiency and selectivity. The use of enzymes in the chemical industry can theoretically enable numerous efficient and sustainable reaction pathways. Nevertheless, the application of enzymes is hindered by their narrow catalytic repertoire. Enzymes are readily deactivated under nonnatural environments, and their reaction types are limited. Developing enzymes with new catalytic functions has been a longstanding challenge in the field of biocatalysis. Strategies such as directed evolution and de novo protein design have been very successful in designing new enzymes. However, as both approaches rely on the engineering of amino acid sequences of proteins, they remain constrained and cannot fully meet the growing demand for non-natural biocatalysis. Incorporating abiotic components with enzymes is a powerful tool for editing enzymes to render new catalytic capabilities. Metal-based components possess a broad catalytic repertoire, structural stability, and multifunctionality, making them promising building blocks for enzyme editing. This Account summarizes our contributions over the past decade in editing enzyme catalysts with metal-based components as a scale-dependent evolution, from nanoscale environmental modulation to atom-scale active site redefinition, illustrating how enzyme editing with metal-based components can systematically address non-natural catalytic challenges. A conceptual framework in which enzymes are edited with metal-based components across scales from the nanometer to the atomic dimension is introduced, establishing a logical basis for integrating biocatalysis with abiotic reactivity. At the nanoscale, enzymes are encapsulated in metal-based frameworks to improve the configuration stability, enabling catalysis under non-native and harsh conditions. The robustness of enzymes under extreme pH, high temperature, and organic solvent can be largely enhanced through the regulation of metal-based frameworks. At the sub-nanoscale, metal clusters are embedded within enzyme scaffolds to construct enzyme-metal hybrid catalysts. By integration of enzymatic and chemical catalysis, new non-natural catalytic processes can be established. At the atomic scale, metal atoms are incorporated into the enzyme catalytic pocket, creating new hybrid active sites. The hybrid active site endows an enzyme with capabilities to drive new-to-nature reactions, unlocking an expanded enzyme catalytic space. This work provides a unifying conceptual framework that clarifies how metal-based components can be strategically employed to reprogram enzyme stability, functionality, and reactivity. We hope that the strategies and concepts discussed herein offer comprehensive design principles for biohybrid catalysts and establish a foundation for reprogramming enzymatic function beyond evolutionary limitations.

records.title: Engineering a hemoglobin variant with enhanced stability and oxygen affinity using a protein language model.
records.abstract: Engineered hemoglobin variants offer therapeutic promise for artificial blood substitutes and oxygen therapeutics, but rational design is constrained by protein stability and heme-binding. Protein language models (pLMs) predict mutation fitness, yet their integration with biophysical validation remains limited. We developed a hybrid pipeline combining pLM (ESM3) with molecular docking, Monte Carlo simulation, molecular dynamics, MM-GBSA/PBSA binding free energy calculations, and density functional theory (DFT) to engineer a stabilized hemoglobin variant (esmHb) with enhanced oxygen affinity, benchmarking against the clinically characterized Hb Fort de France mutation (α45 His→Arg). ESM3 accurately assessed the fitness effect of the Hb Fort de France mutation and generated structurally stable esmHb models. Compared with the wild-type variant (wtHb), esmHb exhibited improved thermodynamic stability (ΔG: -18.48 vs. -12.22 kcal/mol), increased heme-binding affinity (ΔGbind: -11.79 vs. -8.42 kcal/mol), and greater thermodynamic favorability of oxidation according to DFT calculations (ΔE: -173.1 vs. -149.9 kcal/mol). MM-GBSA and MM-PBSA binding free energy calculations further supported improved protein-heme and protein-protein interactions, with esmHb showing more favorable values in both implicit solvation models. Statistical significance (p < 0.05) was reached for protein-protein interactions via both methods and for protein-heme interactions via MM-PBSA. We interpret the MM-GBSA results as a suggestive trend rather than definitive evidence. This work establishes a generalizable framework for pLM-driven protein engineering applicable to therapeutic Hb variants and beyond.

records.title: Advances and applications of engineered protein therapeutics and their role in precision medicine.
records.abstract: Proteins are a vital class of biomolecules. They play essential roles in biological processes, including building cellular structures, forming cellular channels and receptors, catalyzing biological reactions, transporting molecules, and contributing to immune defense mechanisms. Advances in protein engineering have enabled the genetic modification of naturally occurring proteins, using recombinant deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) technology, leading to the development of therapeutic proteins with enhanced specificity, stability, and clinical performance. Despite the rapid growth of engineered biologics, a comprehensive understanding of how these innovations intersect with precision medicine remains limited. This review addresses this gap by summarizing the major contemporary approaches used in therapeutic protein engineering, including directed evolution, rational design, and de novo protein design, and by analyzing their roles in enabling patient-tailored interventions. It provides an integrated overview of the clinical applications of engineered therapeutic proteins across key medical fields, supported by a list of U.S. Food and Drug Administration- and European Medicines Agency-approved protein therapeutics from 2020 to 2025. The review further provides a comparative perspective on major protein engineering strategies, highlighting their relative advantages and limitations, while examining differences in clinical translation across major disease areas. By combining technological advances with disease-specific applications, this review offers a perspective that has not been fully developed in the literature. Finally, the review discusses the current challenges affecting the implementation of precision medicine, including immunogenicity, regulatory constraints, and ethical considerations, and outlines future directions, such as artificial intelligence-guided protein design, targeted protein degradation, and personalized vaccine development. Collectively, these insights highlight the expanding role of engineered proteins in shaping the next-generation of precision therapeutics and emphasize the growing importance of integrating multidisciplinary approaches to advance therapeutic innovation in modern clinical practice.

records.title: APR-Score: Identification and Scoring of Aggregation-prone Regions in Protein Sequences.
records.abstract: Protein aggregation is a critical phenomenon associated with numerous neurodegenerative and systemic diseases. Understanding the propensity of proteins to aggregate is essential for unraveling the molecular basis of these disorders and for the design and engineering of novel proteins, as well as for modulating the activity/stability of enzymatic proteins. Here, we present APR-Score, a novel machine learning-based computational method designed to identify aggregation-prone regions within protein sequences. APR-Score leverages a combination of sequence-based features to predict regions of proteins that are prone to aggregation. It harnessed the information embedded in compiled sequence and structural features to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy. The method was evaluated through rigorous cross-validation on the training dataset and further validated on an independent test dataset. APR-Score demonstrated robustness and reliability in distinguishing aggregation-prone regions from non-aggregating ones, achieving a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.77, precision of 0.89, and F1-Score of 0.87. This tool offers significant value for researchers investigating protein aggregation-related diseases, as it can expedite the identification of aggregation-prone regions, thereby aiding the development of targeted therapies and diagnostic tools. Moreover, computational protein design and engineering efforts can be facilitated by APR-Score-based identification and screening of aggregation-prone protein sequences. APR-Score is available at https://github.com/TII-BRC/APR-Score.

records.title: HDAC8 Assistant: a QSAR-guided molecular generation platform for de novo design and virtual screening of HDAC8 inhibitors.
records.abstract: Histone deacetylase 8 (HDAC8) inhibitors are considered promising therapeutic agents for the treatment of cancer and several other diseases. In this study, regression QSAR models for HDAC8 inhibitors were developed using various types of molecular descriptors and machine learning algorithms. The best-performing weighted consensus model achieved an external predictive performance of Q2test = 0.62 for the complete test set and 0.71 for compounds within the applicability domain, covering 77% of the external data. Model reliability was confirmed by five-fold cross-validation and y-randomization tests. The developed QSAR model was integrated into the HDAC8 Assistant web application (https://hdac8-assistant.streamlit.app/), which includes a de novo molecular generation module based on recurrent neural networks (SMILES-RNN) and reinforcement learning (REINVENT 2). For targeted discovery of novel inhibitors, an original reward function was proposed that combines QSAR-predicted activity with applicability domain control for generated compounds. This approach enables simultaneous optimization of predicted inhibitory activity while limiting extrapolation beyond the model applicability domain. HDAC8 Assistant also implements assessment of drug-likeness according to the Muegge criteria, as well as PAINS, toxicophore, and Brenk structural-alert detection. Molecular docking was performed for the most promising compounds generated by HDAC8 Assistant to analyse their interactions with the HDAC8 active site.

records.title: Programming biological behavior with AI-guided de novo protein design.
records.abstract: Driven by advances in artificial intelligence, de novo protein design can now generate diverse molecular functions from the ground up, achieving remarkable success in engineering binders against many macromolecular targets. Here, we provide a perspective on how de novo design can progress beyond bimolecular interactions toward the bottom-up construction of protein reaction networks. We highlight how programmable, modular, and controllable de novo components can drive complex, emergent biological behaviors. Overcoming current challenges-including designable protein dynamics, multi-step functionalities, and non-equilibrium systems-is essential for this transition. With continued foundational method improvements, the field is poised to pioneer precise protein perturbations for systems-level insight and to engineer emergent cellular behaviors like signal amplification, decision-making, and error correction de novo to fundamentally advance synthetic biology, biotechnology, and medicine.

records.title: Association of Circulating Eosinophils With Systemic Immune Activation and Reduced Recurrence in Hormone Receptor-Positive/Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2-Negative Breast Cancer.
records.abstract: Hormone receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2-) breast cancer, the most common subtype, lacks simple, noninvasive biomarkers for recurrence. We evaluated circulating eosinophil count as a clinically applicable biomarker for recurrence in this population. Associations between preoperative eosinophil count and patient outcomes were evaluated in a multimodal discovery cohort (N = 472) and validated via propensity score overlap weighting in an independent expanded cohort (N = 23,170). We assessed the additive value of eosinophils in patients with 21-gene recurrence scores (RSs; n = 2,973) and their predictive role for adjuvant cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) inhibitors in high-risk patients (n = 3,471). Mechanisms were investigated using integrated multiomics, spatial digital pathology, and in vivo preclinical models. Higher circulating eosinophil counts correlated with significantly improved recurrence-free and distant metastasis-free survival in the discovery cohort. Genomic analysis associated these elevated counts with lower human leukocyte antigen homozygosity and increased intratumoral immune activation. Functionally, eosinophils were associated with antitumor effects, with evidence of CD8+ T-cell involvement. These findings were further validated in vivo, where eosinophil adoptive transfer significantly reduced tumor burden in both the EMT6 (BALB/c) and E0771 (C57BL/6) mouse models. Spatial profiling demonstrated that tumor-infiltrating eosinophils predominantly coaggregated with lymphocytes. These clinical associations were then validated in the independent expanded cohort through multivariable and propensity score-weighted analyses. Critically, eosinophil levels provided additive prognostic value beyond the 21-gene RS and, among high-risk patients, predicted the subset that would derive greater benefit from CDK4/6 inhibition. Circulating eosinophil count serves as a potential clinically applicable, liquid biopsy biomarker that independently prognosticates recurrence risk and predicts CDK4/6 inhibitor benefit, reflecting systemic immune activation in hormone receptor-positive/HER2- breast cancer.

records.title: Site-Specific Outcomes and Genomics in Metastatic Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
records.abstract: Clinical and molecular features of pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) according to involved metastatic sites have not been well characterized. We used the Foundry platform to query information for patients with metastatic PDAC at MD Anderson Cancer Center. Involved metastatic sites were extracted using natural language processing from imaging reports and verified by chart reviews. Overall survival (OS) and next generation sequencing (NGS) data were analyzed. In a cohort of 1,095 patients (median overall survival [OS]: 22.8 months), lung-only metastasis was associated with longer median OS (57.6 months, p<0.0001). Patients with metastases not involving the liver had OS of 41.3 months, while liver-only (19.5 months) and multiple sites including liver (19.3 months) had the poorest survival. TP53 mutation rates were higher in liver-involved groups (84-85%) versus lung-only (73%) and non-liver metastases (67%, p<0.0001). Lower rates of GNAS mutations were detected in liver-only (5%) and liver-involved (2%) cases, higher in lung-only (8%) and non-liver (10%, p<0.01). The frequency of KRAS mutation and mutant allele distribution were not significantly different in tissue based NGS. However, in liquid biopsy analysis (n = 240), lung-only metastasis showed the lowest mutation detection (50%), TP53 (23%) and KRAS (10%), compared to liver-only detection rates of 65%, 46%, and 52% respectively (p values: 0.009, 0.02, <0.001). Patients with PDAC without liver metastasis have significantly improved OS and lower rates of TP53 mutation. Patients with lung-only metastasis had longer OS, a lower liquid-biopsy positivity rate, and a lower rate of KRAS detection by liquid biopsy; because liquid biopsy may under-detect KRAS in lung-only disease, tumor-tissue sequencing should be prioritized in these patients as KRAS-directed therapies emerge.

records.title: Potential Role of BCL2 and BCL6 Overexpression in Circulating Tumor Cells as Molecular Biomarkers in DLBCL After R-CHOP Therapy.
records.abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most prevalent non-Hodgkin lymphoma subtype. Although R-CHOP remains the standard first-line therapy, up to 30% of patients experience relapse or refractory disease. Currently, therapeutic monitoring relies on imaging, which is less sensitive than molecular techniques for detecting residual disease. To evaluate BCL2 and BCL6 oncogene expression in Circulating Tumor Cells (CTCs) as potential molecular biomarkers for clinical outcomes in DLBCL patients after R-CHOP therapy. We analyzed BCL2 and BCL6 expression in CTCs from 42 patients post-R-CHOP using immunomagnetic enrichment of CD20+ cells followed by RT-qPCR. Patients exhibited significantly higher BCL2 (p = 0.003) and BCL6 (p = 0.001) expression than healthy controls. Overexpression of BCL2 and BCL6 was observed in 16.7% and 19% of patients, respectively, with 9.5% showing co-expression. Normal BCL6 expression correlated with complete response (p = 0.004), and BCL6 demonstrated high discriminative ability for disease activity (AUC = 0.791, p = 0.008). The presence of BCL2 and BCL6 in CTCs suggests that liquid biopsy serves as a robust, complementary tool to PET/CT for post-treatment monitoring. These findings support the utility of BCL6 as a biomarker for residual disease surveillance in DLBCL.

records.title: Endometrial cancer molecular classification: research advances and clinical application.
records.abstract: As research in molecular biology continues to advance, the classification of endometrial cancer has gradually shifted from traditional histology toward risk stratification based on the integration of molecular subtyping with clinicopathologic factors. Molecular subtyping has not only transformed our understanding of the biological heterogeneity of endometrial cancer but also provided new evidence for prognostic assessment and treatment selection. However, the maturity of clinical evidence and the translational therapeutic value vary across molecular subtypes. This review systematically summarizes the molecular characteristics and clinical significance of the POLE ultramutated(POLE-mut)subtype, mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) subtype, p53 abnormal (p53-abn) subtype, and no specific molecular profile (NSMP) subtype, with a focus on evaluating whether different molecular features can be further translated from risk stratification into specific treatment decisions. Centering on key issues such as de-escalated therapy for the POLE-mut subtype, the predictive value of immunotherapy for the dMMR subtype, intensified therapy for the p53-abn subtype, and further risk stratification of the NSMP subtype, this review analyzes the clinical basis and limitations of existing evidence and further discusses the challenges that tumors with multiple molecular features pose for classification and treatment decision making. Building on this, the paper compares how major international guidelines integrate molecular information with clinical and pathologic factors and analyzes real world implementation barriers such as testing standardization, result interpretation, and healthcare accessibility. Finally, it outlines the potential value of emerging technologies, including liquid biopsy, artificial intelligence, and multiomics, in dynamic risk assessment and precision therapy. This review aims to trace the continuum of evidence from molecular discovery to clinical action, clarifying which clinical decisions can be supported by existing molecular markers and identifying questions that current evidence cannot yet answer, thereby providing guidance for the precise application and clinical translation of molecular subtyping in endometrial cancer.

records.title: miRNAs bridging the gap between the tumor microenvironment and liquid biopsy in cutaneous melanoma.
records.abstract: Cutaneous melanoma remains one of the most challenging neoplasms and the deadliest form of skin cancer. miRNAs are a class of non-coding RNA molecules found in both tissues and body fluids that can negatively regulate gene expression in eukaryotic cells, playing key roles in health and disease. Dysregulated miRNA levels have been linked to various aspects of melanocytic tumor biology, including the transition from benign to malignant stages, immunosuppression, dissemination, and therapy resistance. Here, we provide a timely review of the roles of miRNAs within the cutaneous melanoma tumor microenvironment, emphasizing their impact on immune cell phenotypes and functions, angiogenesis, innate and adaptive immunity, and immune checkpoint expression to help refine future biomarkers and therapeutic targets in the field. We will also address their roles in circular and long non-coding RNA sponging interactions and the potential for translating miRNAs into clinical practice, given their simultaneous presence in both cutaneous melanoma tissues and liquid biopsies. The main challenges and limitations associated with such a translational approach will also be addressed.

records.title: Multimodal biomarkers for early detection and immunotherapy assessment in hepatocellular carcinoma: integrating liquid biopsy, AI-based imaging and tumor immune profiling.
records.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) commonly develops in chronically diseased liver and remains challenging because of late detection, heterogeneity, recurrence and limited hepatic reserve. Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based combinations improve outcomes in advanced HCC, but durable responses occur in only a subset of patients. This structured narrative review evaluates biomarkers by intended use: surveillance and early detection, pretreatment prognostic stratification, treatment selection, on-treatment monitoring, neoadjuvant response assessment and postoperative minimal residual disease (MRD) detection. Serum alpha-fetoprotein and clinical scores are accessible but largely reflect tumor burden, inflammation or liver function. Cell-free DNA methylation and fragmentomics provide early-detection and tissue-of-origin signals, while circulating tumor DNA tracks molecular burden and clonal evolution. Tissue and spatial profiling clarify immune responsiveness and resistance, whereas radiomics and deep learning noninvasively assess whole-tumor and peritumoral heterogeneity. These modalities are complementary but require distinct evidence standards. Most early-detection studies use case-control or enriched cohorts, and most immunotherapy associations are retrospective, prognostic or monitoring-related. No biomarker yet supports routine selection among ICI regimens. Unlike modality-specific summaries, this review aligns each biomarker with a defined clinical decision and evidentiary category and proposes a longitudinal framework integrating baseline blood, imaging and tissue features with on-treatment dynamics, preoperative reassessment and postoperative molecular surveillance. Clinical translation requires standardized assays, representative multicenter cohorts, locked external validation and biomarker-guided trials demonstrating value beyond established criteria.
